unwired: FAIL: {n} guard(s) are referenced by no workflow —
they can never fail a build, whatever they contain:
unwired_tests: FAIL: {n} self-test(s) are referenced by no workflow —
the guard is checked in CI but its self-test is not, so a
guard that silently stopped detecting anything would still pass:
bare: FAIL: {n} self-test(s) are run without tools/checks/run_suite.sh —
run bare, an assertion calling an undefined helper passes
silently. Invoke them as: bash tools/checks/run_suite.sh <suite>
untested: FAIL: {n} guard(s) have no test_<name>.sh and are not
footer: Two ways to green: (a) wire it up — add a step to the relevant
workflow (guard AND self-test are separate steps), and write the
missing test_<name>.sh covering the clean case plus each failure
mode the guard's header claims; or (b) the guard is obsolete —
then DELETE it, do not leave it in the tree unreferenced. Adding
a name to {exempt_name} is a loosening, not a fix:
that list exists for four historical guards and must only shrink.
text.ok: check_guards_are_wired: OK — {guards} guard(s) wired into a workflow; {exempt} awaiting a self-test (exempt, must shrink).
